newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis end 1/4 point lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis end 1/4 point lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds closed down 1/4 point Tuesday as good technicals helped municipals avoid the sharper losses suffered by U.S. Treasuries.
"(Muni prices) were holding in pretty well this morning, but they've kind of faded in the afternoon," a municipal trader said, adding that the bid side was probably down 1/4 to 3/8 of a point.
A municipal analyst said while the overall market closed down 1/8 to 1/4 point, high-grade issues worsened by two basis points. Dollar bonds ended down 1/8 point, he said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 15/32 at 96-7/32 to yield 6.93 percent in late New York trade.

Early in the session, players took heart from April retail sales figures. The Commerce Department said retail sales fell 0.3 percent last month, exactly in line with expectations. Excluding the automobile component, however, sales fell 0.1 percent, versus forecasts calling for a 0.1 percent rise.
Later, however, the Atlanta Fed business activity index caused some concern, rising to 22.1 in April versus a revised 8.6 in March.
A trader also said this week's inflation data and next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting were being eyed warily.

"We're holding up better because we don't have as much supply around in our market, and there seems to be a reasonable demand," the muni trader said. "But we haven't been inundated with deals this week or last week for that matter."

Looking ahead to Wednesday's economic news, the market is expected to receive the April producer price index. Economists polled by Reuters expect the overall rate to come in unchanged, while the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices is expected to post a 0.1 percent rise.
Tuesday's bid lists were "moderate" the trader said.

"What happens nowadays is some of the stuff people are selling is not as desirable structure-wise, short-calls, so even if you get that for the bid it doesn't necessarily disrupt the entire market," the trader said. "Because the market for good structured paper will hang in there while that other type of paper will weaken."
In new issues, Dillon Read & Co repriced $198 million Ocean County, N.J., Utilities Authority bonds but left the top yield unchanged at 5.45 percent in 2013.
In competitive action, J.P. Morgan Securities Inc won $139 million Cleveland School District notes with a true interest cost of 4.9125 percent.
J.P. Morgan also won $124 million Maricopa County Community College District, Ariz., general obligation bonds at a net interest cost of 5.3218 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday, May 14 are expected to total $505 million in 22 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $267 million in 10 sales, with a $97 million New Hampshire Housing Development Authority deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $238 million are on the schedule. A $65 million Tennessee Housing Development Authority deal at 1030 EDT is the largest.
An additional six sales totaling $284 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Wednesday depending on market conditions.
